transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-15
Start: 11:00 AM ET
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood SE), Maya (Lakeside), Ethan (Lakeside InfoSec), Priya (Lakeside Product), Oliver (Lakeside Compliance)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Lakeside's data residency and compliance constraints for potential Redwood deployment - evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key concerns: GDPR/data residency for EU customers, HIPAA for certain product lines, log retention & redact requirements, KMS/HSM integration, audit trails and contract language.

Topics:
- Current infra and where customer data currently lives
- Regulatory scope (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI, FFIEC guidance)
- Logging & telemetry restrictions (no raw transcripts in long-term logs)
- Deployment models: hosted API, dedicated GPU pools, private VPC/on-prem
- Next steps: docs, pricing, benchmark plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Jordan, I'll run the intro. Uh, Samira and Diego from our engineering team are on as well. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Maya (Lakeside): Good, thanks. Appreciate you fitting this in. We've got a few folks from product and compliance on the line.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda: data residency, logging/compliance constraints, and what would need to happen to pilot. Ethan, could you share the regulatory scope?
[00:20] Ethan (Lakeside InfoSec): Yeah, sure. We're a regional bank with customers in US and EU - so GDPR's a hard requirement for EU customers, obviously. We also have certain product lines that touch healthcare data for a small portfolio, so HIPAA could apply. PCI for payments is handled by a separate stack but we need to ensure tokens exchanged with any LLM service don't leak.
[00:38] Samira (Redwood SE): Thanks, Ethan. A couple clarifying Qs: when you say GDPR, do you require EU-only processing for EU customer records, or is pseudonymization / contractual safeguards acceptable?
[00:48] Ethan: Good question. For some datasets we need EU processing - residency in EU region. For others, contractual safeguards and SCCs might suffice but we'd prefer data never leave EU for those customers.
[00:58] Priya (Product): Just to add, latency matters for from-product features. If we route EU traffic to EU Dedicated or Private deployment, that's fine but we need to understand cost delta.
[01:07] Diego (Redwood SE): Understood. We support region pinning for Dedicated and Private - we can run Dedicated capacity in eu-west or customer-managed VPC. For Hosted, we have region endpoints but logs and telemetry typically flow through our control plane unless you choose Private.
[01:21] Oliver (Compliance): What about logs? We cannot have long-lived transcripts containing customer PII in logs - retention needs to be limited and redactable.
[01:30] Samira: Totally. We have per-tenant log retention settings and redact hooks; also options to disable certain debug logging. For regulatory customers we typically recommend Dedicated or Private and KMS integration for encryption at rest and key control.
[01:45] Ethan: Can you explain KMS integration - we need to know if we can control keys (bring-your-own-key) and if HSM-backed keys are supported.
[01:52] Jordan: Yes. We support BYOK via standard cloud KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. For Dedicated we can offer customer-managed KMS in some contracts - we'll confirm specifics in the security doc.
[02:05] Maya: Another point: audit logs - we need immutable audit trails showing who accessed model outputs and admin actions.
[02:11] Samira: We emit audit logs for admin actions, deployments, and API key usage. For Private, logs can be routed to your SIEM; for Dedicated we can provide pushed logs or direct S3 export. There's also field-level redaction for transcripts before storage.
[02:28] Priya: On the product side, is there a way to avoid sending raw PII to the model? We've heard of prefix filtering and client-side redaction.
[02:35] Diego: Yes - typical patterns: client-side redaction, tokenization, or our prefix caching and prompt templating. We can also run a preprocessor step in your environment for PII removal; for Private that runs fully in your VPC.
[02:49] Ethan: For HIPAA workloads, we'd want BAA. Do you offer BAAs?
[02:53] Jordan: We do engage on BAA for qualified workloads on Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers - we can discuss case-by-case; generally Dedicated or Private are the recommended paths for PHI.
[03:05] Maya: Could you outline tradeoffs in cost and ops between Dedicated and Private?
[03:10] Samira: Sure - Dedicated is reserved GPU pools managed by Redwood but isolated logically; lower operational overhead and faster time-to-value. Private gives you customer-managed control plane, VPC peering or on-prem; more control over egress, keys, and logs but higher setup time and recurring costs. We can share a cost model spreadsheet.
[03:28] Priya: For EU residency, if we do Dedicated in eu-west, does Redwood still see logs in the US?
[03:33] Diego: For Dedicated instances we can ensure control plane and logs are regionalized, but we need to confirm export paths. For Private, all control plane interactions can be kept in your VPC or on-prem so Redwood doesn't have direct access to raw transcripts. We'll send a region-specific architecture doc.
[03:48] Ethan: On data retention: can we set 0 retention for transcripts and only store telemetry aggregated metrics?
[03:54] Samira: Yes, retention policies are configurable per tenant. We can set minimal retention or immediate purge, and keep aggregated metrics for billing. For high-security customers we disable transcript logs altogether and push only anonymized metrics.
[04:05] Jordan: Any display questions about model explainability or outputs stored for evals?
[04:09] Oliver: We want a way to run evals without storing PII - snapshotting only hash or salted IDs of prompts.
[04:15] Diego: We support hashed prompt IDs and masked examples for evals; we can share our eval pipeline best practices.
[04:22] Maya: A practical constraint: our legal team needs contract language on data residency and breach notification windows. What's Redwood's standard?
[04:30] Jordan: We'll share standard SLA and security addenda. Breach notification windows follow industry norms - 72 hours for incidents we control; for Private deployments where you control infra it's different. We'll include specifics in the security pack.
[04:43] Priya: Regarding competitors - we've been looking at Anthropic and some in-house options; we need to justify cost and reliability.
[04:50] Samira: We can run a short benchmark: 1) latency and cost per token for your sample workload in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, 2) feasibility of KMS/HSM integration and log routing.
[05:00] Ethan: For the benchmark we'll provide a stripped dataset. Can Redwood guarantee masked logs during the run?
[05:06] Diego: Yes, we can run the test in a sandbox with redact hooks and limited retention; we'll document exact retention and delete afterwards.
[05:16] Jordan: Recap of action items - we'll send SOC2/ISO doc, KMS/HSM notes, and a cost model. We should have a deeper infra-focused session with your cloud ops next week if that's okay.
[05:28] Maya: That works. Would also like to involve legal to review the BAA and data residency clauses.
[05:34] Jordan: Sounds good. Any final Qs?
[05:36] Oliver: One small one - do you have examples of customer attestations for EU residency?
[05:40] Samira: We can share redacted case studies and architecture diagrams.
[05:44] Priya: Great. Thanks everyone.
[05:47] Jordan: Thanks all - we'll follow up with docs and schedule.

End of transcript.
